set.body:
Successor split from bd-01M2GTMY1KYB94RGJARBB1GBK8, closed 2026-09-30 by owner decision after packets 1-4 (local main 6c3cb4fb..d9c08120; receipts docs/verification/threshold-*-20260930.md).

Admitted there: MaxT and WestfallYoung for voxel-level FWER under sign-flip-exchangeable nulls, including strong control in the tested partial nulls; HierScan for region-level FWER, empirically calibrated (complete-null bound <= gamma*alpha proven; no strong-control proof; reject can contain null voxels inside a significant region). TFCE, cluster-FDR, RFT and voxelwise FDR are not implemented and not advertised.

Remaining scope:
- Propagate supported first-level uncertainty into group-level thresholding and calibrate it. This depends on first-level SE provenance work.
- Admit or refuse non-uniform and adaptive HierScan priors beyond the tested case (one non-uniform prior with eta 1), under a predeclared protocol with a fresh held-out seed.
- Qualify or explicitly refuse non-symmetric error distributions, where sign flips are invalid, including the null family each design needs.
- Source-bound consumer evidence: a p-value, cutoff, mask, legend and native-result round trip through a real consumer. UMVPA-M4.08 is the expected first consumer.
- Admit or remove the unused PSide and StatKind.T.df.
- Upstream: neurothresh 0.1.0 wy_stepdown crashes on a single test column. The reproducer is in docs/verification/threshold-hierscan-alignment-20260930.md.
- Edge divergences from hier_descend to decide: child-mass > vs >=, singleton-bbox children, and minVoxels default 1 vs 8.

This successor does not block UMVPA-M4.08. M4.08 builds on the admitted methods and should supply the consumer evidence.
set.title: Threshold: first-level uncertainty, prior admission, non-symmetric errors, and consumer evidence
